description: Canonical cross-SDK API surface for the shared AFDATA contract (protocol builders/reader, output, redaction, CLI primitives, core types). The closed-world CliSpec compiler and help-v2 are the only lifecycle/help contract; the Rust reference ships first. Skill administration, tracing, stream redirection, and the whole `document` module are Rust-only and outside this manifest, so the checked count is the shared contract, not the crate's full public surface. A null entry means that language has no required top-level export for the group; the note records the idiomatic equivalent or the deliberate contract gap. Reverse export checks still reject undeclared public symbols. Validated by scripts/validate_api_surface.py, wired into scripts/test.sh's static phase.

groups.note: Rust-only stable public domain-error declaration. It deliberately has no runtime diagnostic field.
Rust-only validated lookup table that builds protocol error events from ErrorSpec by stable code.
Rust-only duplicate/unknown/invalid catalog error.

Rust-only typed protocol-validation error (stable rule slug + JSON pointer + message) returned by validate_protocol_event/validate_protocol_stream. Python/TS/Go SDKs still surface validation failures as a plain message (ValueError / Error / error), not yet upgraded to the typed violation — a tracked cross-SDK gap.
Rust/TS/Go use a decoded-event enum/union/interface; Python returns one of DecodedResult/DecodedError/DecodedProgress/DecodedLog directly without a wrapping union type.

The single value × format × options → String entry point. Replaces the former output_json/output_yaml/output_plain (+ _with_options) and cli_output/cli_output_with_options families. Rust/Go take an explicit OutputOptions argument (OutputOptions: Default); Python/TS keep it an optional keyword/parameter.

Explicit URL-only prose helper. It recognizes complete scheme-prefixed URL spans and delegates URL redaction; ordinary structured redaction never scans arbitrary prose.

Rust/Go also expose it as a configured Redactor method (.argv()/.Argv()) for custom secret_names/policy; Python/TS take secret_names/policy as keyword arguments, matching redacted_value/redact_url_secrets.

Rust/Go use a configured Redactor value (.value()/.url() or .Value()/.URL()) for custom secret_names/policy; Python/TS take secret_names/policy as keyword arguments directly on redacted_value/redact_url_secrets/OutputOptions instead of a separate type.

Rust/Python/TS construct via CliEmitter's own constructor (CliEmitter::new / CliEmitter(...) / new CliEmitter(...)), not a separate top-level export. Go has no constructor methods, so this is a free function.
Go-only free constructor (Go has no constructor methods); Rust/Python/TS use CliEmitter::with_options / CliEmitter(..., options=...) / new CliEmitter(..., options) instead.
Rust/Python expose this as the OutputTo::parse associated function / OutputTo.parse classmethod, not a separate top-level export; Go/TS provide it as a free function.

Go-only free constructor for a finite one-shot emitter (result to stdout, error/progress/log to stderr); Rust/Python/TS construct via CliEmitter methods (finite / finite_with / finiteWith), not separate top-level exports.
Go-only free constructor: finite one-shot emitter with explicit output options; Rust/Python/TS use CliEmitter's finite constructor with an options argument instead.

Go-only free constructor that builds a finite (split) or unified emitter from a parsed OutputTo selector, wired to the process streams; Rust/Python/TS use CliEmitter::from_output_to / from_output_to / fromOutputTo methods.
Go-only free constructor: from-OutputTo with explicit output options; Rust/Python/TS use the from_output_to method with an options argument instead.

Python exposes this as a classmethod (OutputOptions.for_policy). Rust has no such function: it implements `From<RedactionPolicy> for OutputOptions`, so the equivalent is `OutputOptions::from(policy)` or `policy.into()`.
TS-only structural type for the writer CliEmitter accepts; Rust expresses the equivalent as a generic bound (W: Write), Python/Go accept any writable/file-like object without naming the shape.
TS-only exported type alias for a JSON value. Rust uses serde_json::Value (from the serde_json crate, not this crate's own naming); Python/Go use the host language's dynamic Any/any.
Rust-only: a typed write-failure error for CliEmitter. Python/TS/Go raise/return the host language's native I/O error instead.

Rust-only writer for the raw documents the CliSpec compiler injects into every registry (--docs Markdown, --output plain help, shell scripts): it owns stream routing and the rule that a closed reader is success. The other SDKs have no CliSpec compiler yet (see cli_spec), so they produce none of those outcomes and need no writer for them; add it there alongside the deferred compilers.
